description: As the indisputable father of Western philosophy, Socrates stands as the archetype of free inquiry and intellectual honesty throughout history. He dared to explore the minds of men, to analyse the content of cherished beliefs, and to distinguish knowledge and truth from opinion. This philosophical gadfly irritated the people of Athens, who tried him for corrupting their youth, and subsequently sentenced him to death for his "crime". In these four short works by Plato, we come to experience the full range of Socrates' penetrating mind. In the "Euthyphro", Socrates searches after the truth about the nature of piety, even as he makes his way to Athens to answer an indictment levelled against him. "The Apology" recounts Socrates' attempt to defend himself against the charge of impiety. Once condemned, Socrates finds himself imprisoned to await death. "The Crito" captures his views on his relationship with the state and what each has a right to expect from the other. Finally, the "Phaedo" recalls the death scene as Socrates discusses the nature of the soul and immortality just before succumbing to the hemlock. -- Back cover

docs.description: Journal, kept by Daniel L. Tinkham, comprised of two whaling voyages. First voyage documents the Samuel and Thomas (Bark) of Mattapoisett, Mass., mastered by Ephraim Poole, from 3 September 1852 - 1 September 1854 in the North Atlantic Ocean. Describes three months of outgoing voyage. There are few coordinates; wind, weather, and ship's heading are included. Pages 26-36 include accounts, pencil sketches of houses, numbers, and names. The voyage was for sperm whales and blackfish. Lowered for both with no success. Recruited men in the Azores and Cape Verde Islands for this voyage. Second voyage documents the March (Brig) of Mattapoisett, Mass., mastered by Henry Lewis,from 21 June 1855 - 12 August 1856 to the North and South Atlantic Ocean for sperm whales and blackfish. Logbook contains ships seen and spoken, profile views of Faial, Pico, and the Canary Islands, calligraphy, ink sketches of the ship, whales and people. Also contains watercolors of whaling scenes. At one point "All hands at work making bird cages."
